pages.hook: American cities are often built in blocks, so people explain distance with blocks and minutes. Asking a stranger for help is normal and usually friendly.
pages.polite: Start with **“Excuse me”** and finish with **“Thank you so much!”** It sounds polite and natural.

mythfact.s: Main Street is a very common street name in the USA.
mythfact.why: Many American towns have a Main Street in the center.

mythfact.s: The post office in the USA is called USPS.
mythfact.why: USPS means United States Postal Service.

mythfact.s: Nobody in the USA uses ATMs.
mythfact.why: ATMs are everywhere, and many work 24 hours.

mythfact.s: People give directions only in kilometers.
mythfact.why: The USA uses miles, blocks and walking minutes.

decode.q: Can you use the ATM at night?

pages.title: Reading quest — A stranger asks for help · part 1
text: Evan was new in Chicago. He had a map on his phone, but the battery was dead. He needed the bank, so he asked a woman on the corner, “**Excuse me, where is the bank?**”
She smiled. “**It’s on Main Street**,” she said. “Is it far?” Evan asked. “**No, it’s five minutes on foot**,” she answered. “You can walk there.”

Evan looked at the street. There was a pharmacy on the left and a small café on the right. “Is it next to the post office?” he asked. “**Yes, it’s next to it**,” she said. “The post office has a big blue sign.”

pages.title: Reading quest — A stranger asks for help · part 2
text: “**Thank you so much!**” Evan said. “**You’re welcome. Have a nice day!**” she said. “**Good luck! It’s easy to find**.” Evan felt happy. People in this city were friendly.
He walked past the café, past the pharmacy and saw the blue sign. Next to it was the bank, a tall gray building. It was open, and the door was heavy.
Inside, a man at the desk said, “Good morning. How can I help you?” Evan took a deep breath and began to speak slowly, in clear English.
